- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later days.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 75–80 range), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture this “rebound” or “mean reversion” effect.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the latter half of the 30-day forecast, particularly after day 15–20.
- Model often fails to adjust for strong downward momentum in the history — e.g., when prices drop from 70+ to 60+, model doesn’t sufficiently reduce forecast.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of downward corrections after spikes — e.g., 80 → 60 is not fully reflected in forecast.
- Model shows “lag” in reacting to recent price drops — forecasts still show higher values than true outcome for 3–5 days after a drop.
- Model tends to overfit recent high prices (e.g., 75–80) and fails to anticipate subsequent correction — especially in the 20–30 day horizon.
- Model exhibits “mean reversion” bias — forecasts too often assume prices will return to historical mean (e.g., 65–70) too quickly, without accounting for volatility or structural shifts.
